title: U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee
text:
ECONOMIC GROWTH ANALYSIS



The principal comparison is 2010–2024. GDP values are nominal dollars, and GDP per capita divides each state-industry value by that state’s estimated population.

MATTHEW BUTERA PYTHON / TABLEAU

title: U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee
text:
1. State growth
The first comparison identifies the states with the strongest economic growth from 2010 to 2024. Nominal GDP growth measures growth in total economic output, while GDP per capita accounts for differences in population size.


Show code
gdp_2010 = gdp_df.loc[gdp_df['YEAR'] == 2010].drop(columns=['YEAR','EST_POP','OVERALL_GDP','BEA_REGION']).rename(columns={'GDP': 'GDP_2010', 'GDP_CAPITA':'GDP_CAPITA_2010'})
gdp_2024 = gdp_df.loc[gdp_df['YEAR'] == 2024].drop(columns=['YEAR','EST_POP','OVERALL_GDP','BEA_REGION']).rename(columns={'GDP': 'GDP_2024', 'GDP_CAPITA':'GDP_CAPITA_2024'})

gdp_change = gdp_2010.merge(gdp_2024, on=[
        'REGION_NAME',
        'STATE/REGION',
        'NAICS',
        'NAICS_LDESC',
        'LEVEL'])
gdp_change['GDP_GROWTH'] = (gdp_change['GDP_2024'] - gdp_change['GDP_2010']) / gdp_change['GDP_2010'] * 100
gdp_change['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / gdp_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100
gdp_change = gdp_change.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

top_state_gdp = (gdp_change
    .loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0']
    .sort_values(by='GDP_GROWTH', ascending=False)
    .head(10)[['REGION_NAME','GDP_GROWTH']])

top_state_capita = (gdp_change
    .loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0']
    .sort_values(by='CAPITA_GROWTH', ascending=False)
    .head(10)[['REGION_NAME','CAPITA_GROWTH']])










Figure 1





Utah led both rankings, with nominal GDP growth of 153.2% and GDP-per-capita growth of 100.6%. Washington was a close second in per-capita growth, at 100.3%.

title: U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee
text:
2. Industry growth
To understand what’s behind this, the following charts move from broad sector groups to sectors and subsectors, then show where the fastest-growing sectors expanded most.


Show code
naics_change = (gdp_change
    .groupby('NAICS_LDESC')[['GDP_2010','GDP_CAPITA_2010','GDP_2024','GDP_CAPITA_2024']].sum()
    .reset_index())
naics_change_reg = (gdp_change
    .groupby(['REGION_NAME','STATE/REGION','NAICS_LDESC'])[['GDP_2010','GDP_CAPITA_2010','GDP_2024','GDP_CAPITA_2024']].sum()
    .reset_index())

naics_change['GDP_GROWTH'] = (naics_change['GDP_2024'] - naics_change['GDP_2010']) / naics_change['GDP_2010'] * 100
naics_change['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / naics_change['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100
naics_change_reg['GDP_GROWTH'] = (naics_change_reg['GDP_2024'] - naics_change_reg['GDP_2010']) / naics_change_reg['GDP_2010'] * 100
naics_change_reg['CAPITA_GROWTH'] = (naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2024'] - naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2010']) / naics_change_reg['GDP_CAPITA_2010'] * 100

naics_change['LEVEL'] = naics_change['NAICS_LDESC'].map(level_map)
naics_change_reg['LEVEL'] = naics_change_reg['NAICS_LDESC'].map(level_map)
naics_change_reg['BEA_REGION'] = naics_change_reg['STATE/REGION'].map(bea_regions)



Broad sector-group growth
The broadest industry view shows which combined sector groups produced the strongest nominal GDP growth.
For reference: Trade combines wholesale and retail trade; Manufacturing and information includes manufacturing plus digital knowledge and communication industries.








Figure 2





Arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services recorded the strongest nominal GDP growth, increasing 131.4%. Professional and business services ranked second, at 115.5%.


Sector and subsector growth per capita
The next figure ranks the five fastest-growing sectors and ten fastest-growing subsectors nationwide by GDP-per-capita growth.








Figure 3





The top subsectors revealed the most interesting results. Given the recent growth of AI companies in the last five years (as of 2026), the highest growth was still in AI related subsectors as of the last year in this data (2024).


State leaders within the five fastest-growing sectors
Using the five leading sectors from the previous figure, each panel ranks the ten states with the strongest per-capita growth in that sector.

title: U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee
text:
3. Growth contribution
To estimate how industries contributed to overall growth, each sector’s prior-year share of state GDP is multiplied by its year-over-year growth rate. The resulting measure approximates the percentage points each sector contributed to state GDP growth.
\[
\text{Growth contribution}_{i,t}
= \text{GDP share}_{i,t-1} \times \text{Industry growth rate}_{i,t}
\]
Because 2010 has no prior-year observation, the contribution analysis covers 2011–2024.


Show code
gdp_df = gdp_df.sort_values(by=['STATE/REGION','NAICS','YEAR']).reset_index(drop=True)

gdp_df['YoY CHANGE'] = gdp_df.groupby(['STATE/REGION','NAICS'])['GDP'].pct_change(fill_method=None) * 100
gdp_df['GDP_SHARE'] = gdp_df['GDP'] / gdp_df['OVERALL_GDP']
gdp_df['GDP_SHARE_PY'] = gdp_df.groupby(['STATE/REGION','NAICS'])['GDP_SHARE'].shift(1)
gdp_df['GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION'] = gdp_df['GDP_SHARE_PY'] * gdp_df['YoY CHANGE']

sector_contribution = (gdp_df
    .loc[(gdp_df['LEVEL'] == 2) & gdp_df['YEAR'].between(2011, 2024)]
    .groupby(['NAICS_LDESC'])['GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION']
    .sum()
    .reset_index()
    .sort_values(by='GROWTH_CONTRIBUTION', ascending=False))










Figure 5





These totals aggregate contributions to state economies across multiple years; they rank sectors’ relative influence but do not represent a single national GDP growth rate.

How contribution varies by BEA region
This heatmap compares the contributions of the 12 leading national sectors across the eight BEA regions.
For both heatmaps, compare sectors across each row to identify the strongest contributors within a region or state. Values sum annual percentage-point contributions from 2011–2024 and should not be interpreted as standalone growth rates or used to rank economies.








Figure 6







What drove growth in the leading per-capita states?
This heatmap compares the same 12 sectors across the ten states with the strongest GDP-per-capita growth.








Figure 7

text:
4. International trade
To place domestic growth in an international context, this section examines state import and export data from the U.S. Census Bureau. The first comparison sums trade values by industry from 2010 through 2024.

Overall export and import value
The chart below displays cumulative exports and imports on the same scale to compare both sector size and the balance between the two forms of trade.








Figure 8





Manufactured goods dominated both exports and imports, accounting for approximately $20.0 trillion in exports and $31.5 trillion in imports from 2010 through 2024.


How state trade exposure changed
Trade exposure measures each state’s exports or imports as a percentage of its total GDP. The KPIs below show that export exposure declined in a large majority of states. Among states where import exposure increased, the average rise was about 2 percentage points (a relatively small shift).


Show code
export_change = (exports_df
    .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE'])
    .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2010'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
).merge((exports_df
    .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE'])
    .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2024'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
), on=['STATE/REGION'])

export_change = (export_change
    .merge(gdp_change.loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'][['STATE/REGION','REGION_NAME','GDP_2010','GDP_2024']], on=['STATE/REGION']))
export_change['EXPORT_2010_EXP'] = export_change['EXPORTS_2010'] / export_change['GDP_2010'] * 100
export_change['EXPORT_2024_EXP'] = export_change['EXPORTS_2024'] / export_change['GDP_2024'] * 100
export_change['EXP_GROWTH_PP'] = export_change['EXPORT_2024_EXP'] - export_change['EXPORT_2010_EXP']

import_change = (imports_df
    .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE'])
    .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2010'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
).merge((imports_df
    .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE'])
    .groupby(['STATE/REGION','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2024'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
), on=['STATE/REGION'])

import_change = (import_change
    .merge(gdp_change.loc[gdp_change['NAICS'] == '..0'][['STATE/REGION','REGION_NAME','GDP_2010','GDP_2024']], on=['STATE/REGION']))
import_change['IMPORT_2010_EXP'] = import_change['IMPORTS_2010'] / import_change['GDP_2010'] * 100
import_change['IMPORT_2024_EXP'] = import_change['IMPORTS_2024'] / import_change['GDP_2024'] * 100
import_change['IMP_GROWTH_PP'] = import_change['IMPORT_2024_EXP'] - import_change['IMPORT_2010_EXP']

negative_export_share = (export_change['EXP_GROWTH_PP'] < 0).mean() * 100
positive_import_states = import_change.loc[import_change['IMP_GROWTH_PP'] > 0]
average_positive_import_growth = positive_import_states['IMP_GROWTH_PP'].mean()










Figure 9







Which trade sectors grew fastest?
The final trade comparison ranks export and import sectors by their percentage growth between 2010 and 2024.


Show code
export_change_sec = (exports_df
    .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','EXP_LEVEL'])
    .groupby(['EXP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2010'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
).merge((exports_df
    .loc[(exports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (exports_df['EXP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~exports_df['EXP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','EXP_LEVEL'])
    .groupby(['EXP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['EXPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'EXPORT_VAL':'EXPORTS_2024'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
), on=['EXP_NAICS_DESC'])

import_change_sec = (imports_df
    .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2010) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','IMP_LEVEL'])
    .groupby(['IMP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2010'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
).merge((imports_df
    .loc[(imports_df['YEAR'] == 2024) & (imports_df['IMP_LEVEL'] == 2) & (~imports_df['IMP_NAICS'].isin(manufacturing_codes))]
    .drop(columns=['GDP_CODE','IMP_LEVEL'])
    .groupby(['IMP_NAICS_DESC','YEAR'])['IMPORT_VAL'].sum()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={'IMPORT_VAL':'IMPORTS_2024'})
    .drop(columns=['YEAR'])
), on=['IMP_NAICS_DESC'])

export_change_sec['EXP_SECT_GROWTH'] = (export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2024'] - export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2010']) / export_change_sec['EXPORTS_2010'] * 100
import_change_sec['IMP_SECT_GROWTH'] = (import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2024'] - import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2010']) / import_change_sec['IMPORTS_2010'] * 100

top_export_growth = export_change_sec.sort_values(by='EXP_SECT_GROWTH', ascending=False).head(5)
top_import_growth = import_change_sec.sort_values(by='IMP_SECT_GROWTH', ascending=False).head(5)










Figure 10





Oil, gas, minerals, and ores was the fastest-growing export sector, rising 669.8%. Among imports, used or second-hand merchandise and returned or reimported goods recorded the two largest percentage increases, at 153.3% and 147.3%, respectively. These rankings reflect percentage growth rather than total trade value.

title: U.S. GDP Growth, Industry Change, Trade, and Tennessee
text:
5. Tennessee
Tennessee ranked among the top ten states in both total GDP growth and GDP-per-capita growth. This section identifies the sectors where Tennessee was a top-five state nationally and shows how broad sector groups contributed to its year-over-year GDP growth.








Figure 11






Tennessee’s growth-contribution timeline
The stacked bars show how broad sector groups combined to produce Tennessee’s annual GDP growth. Positive segments added to growth; negative segments offset it. Durable and nondurable manufacturing are excluded because they overlap the combined manufacturing-and-information group.








Figure 12





After 2020, finance, insurance, real estate, rental, and leasing was Tennessee’s most consistent source of growth, contributing approximately 1.4 to 1.9 percentage points annually through 2024. Arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services also rebounded sharply from its 2020 decline. Its average contribution during 2021–2024 was roughly three times its pre-2020 average.

To see more detail and explore how economic growth changed by state, industry, and year, use the interactive Tableau dashboard.


Sources: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis state GDP data and U.S. Census Bureau state import and export data, using the prepared project files in this repository.
